questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Most crucially for me was an interesting city/culture, that I could get an insight into and immerse myself in.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Bologna University is a jungle, in regards to the bureaucracy and in general getting to know the ins and outs of the university! Though it's often complicated everything works out in the end and you don't need to stress over it.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I received the possibility to be connected with another student, though this program never came through. I was checked in virtually (Corona) and I was giving all the information I needed to start.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I used Airbnb, their is a lot of expats coming through the city so demand for housing is high and the rent likewise.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Get started early if you want to make a good deal.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: At bologna it is possible to change courses at any given time - very different from Copenhagen Uni, but overall I found the possibility of changing courses during the teaching period to be nice as it allowed me to get a sense of a teacher before committing to a course.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: The Erasmus desk was helpfull in changing courses.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got all the classes I wanted.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Try out different classes, you don't have to commit before hand!

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I found the courses to be less demanding then that of Copenhagen Uni

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Less breaks, at Copenhagen Uni, we run a tight shift of 45 min of teaching 15 min break. At bologna a teacher could go non-stop for an hour or more and only give 5 min breaks. This could become very taxing, especially if I had more than one course a day. All courses was 3 hours of teaching, I'm more used to 2 hours of teaching.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
ADVANCED TIME SERIES ECONOMETRICS
ECONOMIC EVALUATION AND HEALTH
FINANCIAL PRODUCTS AND MARKETS
INDUSTRIAL ORGANIZATION: THEORY AND APPLICATIONS
SUPPORTING MANAGERIAL DECISIONS THROUGH MACHINE LEARNING: A PRIMER ON PYTHON

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
ADVANCED TIME SERIES ECONOMETRICS - if you want to go hard on time series econometrics and bootstrapping.

SUPPORTING MANAGERIAL DECISIONS THROUGH MACHINE LEARNING: A PRIMER ON PYTHON - for an easy course for introducing python.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: I spent a lot on traveling, and train tickets in Italy are unexpectedly inexpensive!

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Bikes are dirt cheap in Bologna! Would recommend to buy one!

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Bologna had a lot of sport clubs, but it requires a medical certificate to be a part of.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Theres a few different Erasmus groups creating different experiences for Erasmus students everything from travels to italien language classes.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Take italian lessons, you patience will be rewarded!

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer:
Travel around italy, trains are cheap and quick! You can get to rome in 2 hours using the speedtrain from bologna.
Run or bike in the hills!

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Sport clubs or studen clubs. A lot of politics in bologna, easy to meet other italien students if you get involved

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: None

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The food, and drinks!

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Things are more relaxed at Bologna University in regards to deadlines, adapt to the Italien way by knowing that everything will get done, it'll just take some time.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Read about bologna, the cuisine and the region and you will be rewarded when finding nice restaurant and cities to visit on the weekend.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Learning and immersing myself in italian culture.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The differences in how things a done administratively between bologna and copenhagen.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
